_meta.about: The four horns of legend (src/horns.py, src/game_horns.py). Each is a carried artifact (data/items/artifact.json) that comes only through its story path (data/flavor_encounters.json; the three new paths are placed once a run by karma_rules.json run_start_schedule, the Olifant by Roland's own chain). Its power is in the V menu while it is carried: a HISTORY escalator chain whose length sets how many answer (allies_by_chain, indexed by the chain, 0 to 5). Every horn sounds ONCE A RUN (Brandon, 2026-11-16: 'once per game... must not be game-breaking'), and a failed quiz still spends it. The allies are monster kinds in data/monsters.json (is_allied, quest_only, min_level 0: never found, never spawned) whose numbers are their own, written from their lore at their horn's tier; they walk beside the hero as helpers that come and go (horns.CalledAlly, a Pet), stay 'turns', then leave with their line. They never strike a gate's guardian (the five gate bosses of data/domains.json): the gate's own quest rules decide that fight (Fenrir: Gleipnir binds him, the Sandal ends him; Brandon 2026-11-16). They stay on the floor they were called to.

sources.robin_hoods_horn: Child Ballad 125, Robin Hood and Little John (the bridge, the staves, Robin knocked into the brook, the horn, John Little renamed Little John); Child 123, Robin Hood and the Curtal Friar (Robin asks to blow his horn and his yeomen come; the friar is Friar Tuck); Child 120, Robin Hood's Death (at Kirklees he blows three weak blasts and Little John comes); A Gest of Robyn Hode (Lincoln green; Much the Miller's son; Will Scarlok); Robin Hood and Allen a Dale (the minstrel). Checked on Grokipedia (Little John; Merry Men; Robin Hood's Death), then Wikipedia (Robin Hood and Little John; Robin Hood and the Curtal Friar; Robin Hood's Death), 2026-11-16.
sources.arthurs_bugle: The Sewingshields legend: John Hodgson, History of Northumberland (1840), and The Denham Tracts vol. 2, ed. James Hardy (Folklore Society, 1895), pp. 125-27, retold in D. L. Ashliman, Sleeping Hero Legends (University of Pittsburgh): a farmer knitting on the ruins follows his rolling ball of thread into a vaulted hall with a fire burning without fuel, Arthur, Guinevere, the court and the hounds asleep, and a sword, a garter and a bugle-horn on a table; he draws the sword and they wake, cuts the garter, sheathes the sword and they sleep again; Arthur's rhyme ends 'But never blew the bugle-horn'. Also pantheon.org, Sewingshields Castle. Grokipedia has no page on it (searched 2026-11-16).
sources.gjallarhorn: Snorri Sturluson, Gylfaginning 27 (Heimdall: the white god, gold teeth, dwells at Himinbjorg by Bifrost, watchman of the gods against the mountain giants, needs less sleep than a bird, sees a hundred leagues by night as by day, hears grass grow and wool on sheep; Gjallarhorn is heard in all worlds) and 51 (at Ragnarok he blows it and wakes all the gods; he and Loki kill each other; the wolf swallows Odin; his son tears the wolf apart); Voluspa 46 ('loud blows Heimdall, the horn is aloft'); Grimnismal and Gylfaginning 38-41 (the einherjar: the chosen dead of Valhalla, who fight every day and rise whole at evening, 540 doors and 800 through each at Ragnarok). Checked on Grokipedia (Gjallarhorn; Heimdall; Einherjar; Vidarr), then Wikipedia (Heimdall), 2026-11-16.
sources.olifant: The Song of Roland (Oxford manuscript), laisses 83-85 (Oliver asks Roland three times to sound the olifant) and 133-135 (Roland sounds it; the sound carries thirty leagues; Ganelon tells Charlemagne it is nothing; Duke Naimes says Roland is in battle; the host turns back) and the pursuit and Baligant battle after (Naimes, Ogier the Dane, Geoffrey of Anjou; Charlemagne's sword Joyeuse). Checked on Wikipedia (The Song of Roland) and translations found by search (shmoop, longlongtimeago, Fordham Medieval Sourcebook), 2026-11-16; Grokipedia has no page under that title.

_meta.numbers: Sized for one call that helps through one hard fight at the horn's tier (a war-band, a mini-boss, a seal demon), never a gate. Every stay is ten turns (Brandon, 2026-11-16: the 25 and 30 turns 'may be too strong... maybe 10 turns'): the whole band, at blows about three turns in five, deals about four or five ordinary monsters' health of its tier over its stay (floor_curve.HP_ANCHORS at floors 15, 50, 75 and 90; it was about twelve at the old stays), a war-band's followers or a third of a mini-boss, and each ally lives through about eight blows of a mini-boss of that tier. The allies' own numbers did not change with the stay. The numbers are written in monsters.json; nothing scales them by the floor (LORE, NOT FLOOR), so Robin Hood's men, mortals at tier one, matter less the deeper they are called.

robin_hoods_horn.name: Robin Hood's Horn
robin_hoods_horn.label: Blow Robin Hood's Horn
robin_hoods_horn.desc: His Merry Men come out of the greenwood to fight beside you for a while. Once a run.
robin_hoods_horn.title: ROBIN HOOD'S HORN

lines.raise: You set Robin Hood's horn to your lips and blow.
lines.fail: The note cracks and dies in the dark, and nobody comes. The horn will not sound for you again.
lines.arrive: Men in Lincoln green come out of the dark as if out of the trees of Sherwood: {who}.
lines.leave: {name} raises a hand to you and goes back into the greenwood.
lines.chronicle: Blew Robin Hood's horn. His men came: {who}.
lines.chronicle_fail: Blew Robin Hood's horn badly. Nobody came.

arthurs_bugle.name: Arthur's Bugle
arthurs_bugle.label: Blow Arthur's Bugle
arthurs_bugle.desc: The sleepers under the hill wake to fight beside you for a while. Once a run.
arthurs_bugle.title: ARTHUR'S BUGLE

lines.raise: You set Arthur's bugle to your lips and blow.
lines.fail: Your breath catches in the old horn and the note is gone before it is out of it. Far off, something turns over in its sleep and is still.
lines.arrive: The air rings like a struck bell, and the sleepers come out of it awake and armed: {who}.
lines.leave: {name} bows his head to you and is gone, back to sleep under the hill.
lines.chronicle: Blew Arthur's bugle in need. The sleepers came: {who}.
lines.chronicle_fail: Blew Arthur's bugle too weakly. The sleepers slept on.

gjallarhorn.name: Gjallarhorn
gjallarhorn.label: Blow Gjallarhorn
gjallarhorn.desc: The einherjar ride out of Valhalla to fight beside you for a while. Once a run.
gjallarhorn.title: GJALLARHORN

lines.fail: The great horn only groans, and far above you nobody wakes. It will not sound for you again.
lines.arrive: The note goes up through every floor above you and into Valhalla, and its doors open. Down out of the light ride {who}, Odin's chosen dead.
lines.leave: {name} turns back toward the light. He will fight again tomorrow, and stand up whole at evening.
lines.chronicle: Blew Gjallarhorn. The einherjar came from Valhalla: {who}.
lines.chronicle_fail: Blew Gjallarhorn, but it groaned. Nobody in Valhalla heard it.

olifant.name: The Olifant
olifant.label: Blow the Olifant
olifant.desc: Charlemagne's host rides from far off and comes late: blow it early, then fall back. Once a run.
olifant.title: THE OLIFANT

lines.raise: You set the Olifant to your lips and blow, as Roland did, until your temples ache.
lines.fail: The crack in the mouthpiece takes the note, and it dies in the pass. Nobody far off hears it.
lines.far: Thirty leagues off, an emperor hears it. A traitor tells him it is nothing; his oldest duke tells him no man blows like that unless he is fighting. The host turns back, but it is a long road. Give ground, and hold on until it comes.
lines.on_road: Hooves behind you, a great many of them, and coming hard.
lines.arrive: Charlemagne's host comes up out of the dark at the gallop, too late for Roland and not too late for you: {who}.
lines.chronicle: Blew the Olifant in time. Charlemagne's host came: {who}.
lines.chronicle_fail: Blew the Olifant, but its crack took the note. Nobody far off heard.
